data.title: Virtual Machine Detection
data.summary: The sample queries hardware and firmware identifiers — hypervisor CPUID bits, vendor strings in device and driver names, MAC address OUI ranges — to determine whether it is running inside a virtual machine.
data.description:
Virtual-machine detection is cheaper and more reliable than sandbox detection because the
signals come from the hypervisor itself rather than from an analyst's configuration choices:
the CPUID hypervisor-present bit, vendor strings such as 'VBOX' or 'VMware' surfacing in
registry keys, disk and NIC device names, and ACPI table contents. A sample that only needs
to know 'virtual or not' can get a confident answer from one or two of these.

This is a weaker signal of sophistication than sandbox-specific checks: it fires in genuine
virtualised production estates as well as analysis environments, and a sample that treats
the two identically will sometimes refuse to run on a legitimate virtual desktop.
data.recommendation:
* Where infrastructure is virtualised in production, note that this sample will not detonate there either — plan analysis accordingly.
* Mask or patch the specific hypervisor identifiers checked rather than attempting full bare-metal replication.
* Cross-reference the exact strings checked against the family's other samples; VM-check lists are usually copied wholesale between builds.
data.short_recommendation: Mask the specific hypervisor identifiers checked, or move analysis to bare metal.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Read CPUID leaf 1 ECX bit 31 and queried SCSI device strings for hypervisor vendor names.

mbc_techniques.implementation: CPUID hypervisor-present bit and VirtualBox/VMware device-name strings checked.
